newsitem.title: USA: Calif. 96 onshore oil output up at 263 mln barrels.
newsitem.headline: Calif. 96 onshore oil output up at 263 mln barrels.

text.p: Onshore oil production in California rose to 263 million barrels in 1996, lifted by higher crude oil prices, according to a preliminary report from the state's Department of Conservation.
Production rose by four million barrels, the first year-on-year onshore rise in over a decade, the report said.
"Higher, more stable prices for crude oil made onshore recovery more attractive to producers and helped fuel the production increase," the report said.
Overall state output fell to 347 million barrels in 1996, from 351 million barrels the previous year.
The report attributed the decrease to a sharp drop in production from federal offshoire oil fields, to 64.1 million barrels in 1996, from 74.2 million in 1995.
Final figures will be published later in the 1996 Annual Report of the State Oil and Gas Supervisor.
California ranks fourth among U.S. oil-producing states, behind Texas, Alaska and Louisiana.
Production in California peaked at 423.8 million barrels in 1985 but has since fallen due to less favourable economic conditions and declining reserves, the department said.
